query: In conventional alloys, loss of toughness has long been associated with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation. By contrast, compositionally complex high-entropy alloys can suppress rapid grain coarsening and deleterious intermetallic formation and have shown favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement. These findings do not establish what governs possible toughness degradation in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy. Under the constraint of retaining a compositionally complex alloy suitable for demanding engineering service, what testable mechanistic hypothesis explains whether and why brittle behavior emerges? Specify a controlled comparison that would distinguish the hypothesis from conventional-alloy expectations, predicted observations relative to the initial baseline, its service and loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a decisive falsification outcome.

generation.hypothesis: The emergence of brittle behavior in an initially single-phase high-entropy alloy is governed by the formation of nanoscale precipitates at grain boundaries, which is facilitated by the segregation of specific alloying elements and accelerated by high-temperature exposure.
generation.material_initial_state: Single-phase high-entropy alloy with a compositionally complex structure
generation.conditions: High-temperature exposure in a controlled atmosphere
generation.mechanism: Segregation of specific alloying elements to grain boundaries, leading to the formation of brittle precipitates
generation.predicted_outcome: A 20% decrease in toughness relative to the initial baseline, as measured by Charpy impact testing
generation.baseline: Initial toughness of the single-phase high-entropy alloy
generation.uncertainty: The exact composition and processing history of the alloy may influence the formation and distribution of nanoscale precipitates, affecting the predicted outcome

falsification_experiment.design: Controlled comparison of the high-entropy alloy with a conventional alloy, using advanced analytical microscopies and CALPHAD software to characterize the microstructure and predict phase stability
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the high-entropy alloy exhibits a toughness decrease of less than 10% or greater than 30% relative to the initial baseline, the hypothesis is falsified

prior_attempts: conventional alloys with grain-boundary segregation and brittle grain-boundary precipitation
reason for shortfall: loss of toughness

additional_info.desired_outcome: favorable strength–ductility combinations and resistance to high-temperature softening and low-temperature embrittlement
additional_info.falsification_outcome: observation of brittle behavior inconsistent with the proposed hypothesis
